scope: Compare the current WinUI cash-count preview and request construction with the shared server/domain calculation, denomination endpoint, persistence handler and existing contract tests. This is a semantic mirror/cross-layer consistency check of existing FIN-CAND-CASHCOUNT-001; it is not a new finding or an execution of the original cash-count candidate tests.
decision: For ordinary nonnegative quantities and valid returned denominations within arithmetic range, the client and domain both compute each row as Quantity * DenominationPiastres and sum the rows, so the displayed running total follows the same formula as the server result. The client maps invalid/nonpositive quantity text to zero; the domain clamps negative quantities to zero, which is equivalent for normal UI submissions. SaveAsync sends the denomination rows and expected piastres to the server; the route replaces BusinessDayId from the route, then SaveCashCountHandler calculates and persists the authoritative count plus audit row. The fixed denomination endpoint feeds the normal client, but the POST handler forwards caller-supplied row denominations to CalculateDenominationCount without checking membership in that fixed set. Both client preview and domain calculation multiply long values before summing, and the domain also subtracts expected from total without explicit checked arithmetic. This does not establish differing client/server totals for ordinary valid inputs; the existing cash-count candidate is specifically the server trust/bounds/arithmetic issue, not a separate mirror defect.

manual_reasoning.ui_preview: DenominationRow.Quantity accepts only a parsed positive Int64 and maps invalid, zero, or negative input to 0. CountedTotalDisplay sums each row's long product and formats it for display. SaveAsync requires at least one positive row, parses a nonnegative expected amount, retains an operation ID/request across unresolved outcomes, and sends the row pairs, expected amount, shift/day and current actor ID. The preview is explicitly described as a live aid; server response drives the confirmation text.
manual_reasoning.domain_and_handler: CalculateDenominationCount clamps negative quantities to zero, forms every row total using long multiplication, sums row totals and computes total minus expected. HandleAsync returns an existing count on same-ID replay; otherwise loads the actor, checks cash_count permission, verifies the route-bound day exists, calculates through the domain function, then writes the count and audit event in one SaveChanges call. It does not validate each supplied denomination against EgyptianDenominationsPiastres or bound quantity/expected arithmetic here.
manual_reasoning.endpoint_and_tests: GET cash-count-denominations returns the fixed domain list. POST overwrites request.BusinessDayId from the path and delegates to the handler. Existing integration tests assert a normal two-row total, same-ID idempotent replay, the dedicated permission, and exact fixed denomination list. Those test bodies were read but not run; they do not challenge arbitrary denomination, multiplication overflow, sum overflow or difference overflow.
manual_reasoning.classification: No distinct mirror divergence found for ordinary valid counts. The client and server share the same row-product/sum formula; invalid quantities both normalize to zero. The source-supported candidate remains the existing FIN-CAND-CASHCOUNT-001: request-controlled denomination and unchecked range arithmetic can make persisted calculation invalid for crafted/edge inputs. The normal client gets a finite denomination list, which is counterevidence against a routine UI-triggered unsupported denomination. A route/user authorization issue is outside this comparison and is not re-evaluated here.
manual_reasoning.limitations: Static source and test reading only. No UI, HTTP, SQL, handler, isolated arithmetic harness or test execution in this comparison. The existing candidate pure-calculation artifact is not repeated or reclassified. Some worktree files are CRLF-converted from baseline LF; logical content is identical after newline normalization, and baseline-to-HEAD source diff is empty. Each reference stores exact baseline and worktree SHA-256. No runtime tests performed.
manual_reasoning.recommended_followup: For the existing candidate, define allowed denomination and count/amount bounds at the server boundary and test both authorized HTTP acceptance and rejection in a disposable isolated database; retain valid positive/negative discrepancy controls and request-id replay tests. No implementation performed.

reviewer: Main Codex coordinator; bounded semantic cross-layer comparison; no separate reviewer. Existing independent static challenge status is recorded in the canonical financial candidate/report.
